name: Opobo

summary.text: Founded by Jaja, a former slave who rose to head a Bonny trading house, after he broke with Bonny in 1869. Sitting at the mouth of the Imo river, Opobo took over the palm-oil markets of the hinterland, and Jaja dealt with European firms on his own terms until the British consul deported him in 1887.

snapshots.title: Jaja founds Opobo
snapshots.text: Jaja leads fourteen Bonny houses to a new site at the mouth of the Imo river and names it Opobo.

snapshots.title: Master of the Imo river
snapshots.text: Recognised by Britain in 1873, Opobo controls the palm-oil markets up the Imo river at Essene, Azumini and Akwete, and Jaja ships oil directly to Britain.

snapshots.title: Jaja deported
snapshots.text: Consul Harry Johnston lures Jaja onto a ship and deports him for trying to keep his monopoly. He dies in exile in 1891.

today.text: The Amanyanabo of Opobo, of the Jaja line, reigns in Opobo, Rivers State.
today.title: Amanyanabo of Opobo

reviewNotes: Jaja's deportation date and Johnston's role are taken from general histories; confirm against Dike (1956).
